trial: v8 step 3 -- does Phase 1->2 work outside the synthetic testbed?

target.note: clone only. no patch was generated, applied, committed or pushed.

lenses: A: 契約と型 -- docstring/annotation と実装の不一致
B: 状態と冪等性 -- 呼び出し後にディスク上に残るもの
C: 例外と境界 -- 空・存在しない・symlink・非正規ファイル

findings.claim: `if not src_file` guard is unreachable for the Path half of the declared `Union[str, Path]`: Path('') is PosixPath('.') and is truthy, so get_cache_file_loc(Path('')) returns __pycache__/.cpython-3xx.pyc instead of raising ValueError. The only in-module call site (remove_cfile) always passes a Path, so the guard never fires in production.
findings.oracle: metamorphic: the two spellings of one argument must have the same outcome class
findings.d1_rung: 段2 -- quotable anchor (the annotation and the guard's own message)

findings.claim: docstring `Raises:` lists only FileExistsError; the function also raises ValueError.
findings.why_not: documentation-only. no observable behaviour differs, so no test can fail on it.

findings.claim: check_cache_invalidation_mode docstring says `Returns: None` but returns PycInvalidationMode.TIMESTAMP.
findings.why_not: a test asserting the real return type passes on the current code, so 検査1 cannot hold. Doc bug, not a behaviour bug.

findings.claim: docstring says 'In the directory instance, all cache files are removed'; the implementation enumerates rglob('*.py') and derives each cache file from a SURVIVING source, so a __pycache__ entry whose source was deleted or renamed is left behind.
remove_existing_cache_files silently no-ops for a non-.py file or a path that does not exist (no error, no log).
findings.why_not: no contract text is violated; the tolerance looks intended. This is a proposal, not a fact.

findings.claim: islink is checked before exists, so a broken symlink still raises FileExistsError as documented.
findings.why_not: no defect -- the review claim was disproved by reading.

findings.claim: create_cache_dirs has a TOCTOU window between exists() and mkdir.
findings.why_not: already closed by exist_ok=True. Claim disproved.

yield.caveat: n=7 on one 129-line module. This is a single data point, not a rate.

check1.interpretation: 検査1 holds: T fails on the unfixed code. The deliberate control test (test_live_cache_file_is_removed) passes, so T is measuring the defect and not the fixture.

steps.cost: skipped -- sys.path insertion used instead; `pip install -e .` was avoided so the shared venv is not mutated

2 of 8 test modules (test_cli.py, test_report.py) fail to COLLECT in the shared venv. Did not block this oracle because the anchor module's own tests do not need it, but a full-suite gate (R4/R5) would have started from a red baseline.

an out-of-tree oracle file must be run with --no-cov, otherwise the coverage plugin's config fights the run. The harness assumes it can call pytest with its own flags; this repo's config is not neutral.

steps.step: anchor identification (file:line + the quotable contract text)
steps.cost: the whole of the 25 minutes. Nothing in the harness finds an anchor; a human (or an LLM lens) reads the module.
not exercised -- this trial stopped at 検査1 by design (no patch was produced)

what_this_does_and_does_not_show.shows: the conversion layer (finding -> machine oracle -> 検査1) works on a real repository that the harness has never seen, with no changes to the harness.
what_this_does_and_does_not_show.does_not_show: Phase 3 onwards. No fix was generated and no gate beyond 検査1 was run, so nothing here says the GATES work on this repo -- in particular R4/R5 would have to start from a baseline that already has 2 collection errors.
